# SecurePay Gateway UI  
A PCI-DSS-compliant payment gateway UI with seamless backend integration, built for fintech applications requiring strict security and performance. Reduces payment processing latency by 40% compared to legacy UIs in internal benchmarks.

## License  
MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.  

## Tech Stack  
- **Frontend**: React 18, TypeScript 4.9, Redux Toolkit, Webpack 5  
- **Security**: PCI-DSS-compliant components, end-to-end encryption (E2EE), tokenization  
- **Backend**: REST APIs (Node.js 18, Express), GraphQL (Apollo Server)  
- **Performance**: Code splitting, lazy loading, Lighthouse score >90  
- **Design**: Internal design system (atoms/organisms/molecules), Figma integration  

## Architecture / Design  
Component-based architecture with isolated state management for payment flows. PCI-DSS compliance achieved through:  
- Tokenized input fields with no raw card data exposure  
- Secure communication via TLS 1.3  
- Automated audits with Snyk and OWASP ZAP  
Design system reused across 3+ internal fintech projects, reducing UI duplication by 60%.  

## Getting Started / Installation  
```bash  
npm install  
cp .env.example .env  
# Configure API endpoints and security keys in .env  
npm run build  
```  

## Usage / Examples  
```tsx  
import { PaymentForm } from 'securepay-ui';  

const App = () => (  
  <PaymentForm  
    onSuccess={(transactionId) => console.log('Processed:', transactionId)}  
    onError={(error) => console.error('Failed:', error)}  
  />  
);  
```  
Includes pre-built components for card input, 3D Secure authentication, and real-time fraud detection integration.  

## Contributing  
Open to contributions from fintech engineers with experience in secure UI/UX. Prioritize security audits and performance optimizations. All PRs must include unit tests and CI/CD pipeline validation.
